channel.title: Patrick Henry on Anti-Federalist Library
channel.description: Recent content in Patrick Henry on Anti-Federalist Library

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention I
item.description: Warns that the Constitution contains ambiguous language that could lead to dangerous interpretations and abuses of power.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention II
item.description: Argues that legitimate government must be founded on the consent of the governed and not on the centralization of power.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention III
item.description: Outlines the potential dangers of the proposed government, focusing on its ability to overpower states and infringe on individual rights.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention IV
item.description: Stresses the need for amendments to the Constitution, particularly a Bill of Rights, to protect citizens from government overreach.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention V
item.description: Argues that the process for creating new states from territories could lead to centralized federal control over more land and people.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention VI
item.description: Calls for stronger restraints on government to prevent corruption and protect individual freedoms.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention VII
item.description: Stresses the importance of a well-regulated militia, fearing that the proposed government would weaken state militias and empower a federal army.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention VIII
item.description: Emphasizes the need for officials to be held accountable to the people to prevent the abuse of power.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention IX
item.description: Warns that the Constitution’s provisions could lead to a large standing army, posing a threat to liberty.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention X
item.description: Reaffirms the necessity of state militias for defense and questions the Constitution’s allowance for a federal military monopoly.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XI
item.description: Expresses concern over the federal control of the District of Columbia and its potential to lead to unchecked power.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XII
item.description: Argues strongly for the inclusion of a Bill of Rights to safeguard individual liberties and limit government power.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XIII
item.description: Warns that the Constitution’s implied powers could lead to the expansion of federal authority, including issues like slavery.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XIV
item.description: Emphasizes the risks posed by the Constitution’s lack of explicit protections for habeas corpus and against ex post facto laws.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XV
item.description: Raises concerns about the burdens of both national and state debt under the new Constitution, warning of potential financial crises.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XVI
item.description: Warns that the Constitution’s grant of treaty power to the federal government could lead to the subjugation of state interests.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XVII
item.description: Argues that the ability to make treaties without adequate checks could undermine the sovereignty of the states.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XVIII
item.description: Calls for stricter accountability of government officials to prevent the centralization of power and abuse of office.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XIX
item.description: Highlights the lack of protections for citizens against a potentially oppressive judiciary under the new Constitution.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XX
item.description: Expresses concern that federal courts would become supreme over state courts, eroding state authority and individual rights.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XXI
item.description: Stresses the importance of preserving trial by jury, fearing the Constitution’s provisions would undermine this right.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XXII
item.description: Argues that the enumeration of rights in the Constitution could be misinterpreted or insufficient to fully protect individual liberties.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XXIII
item.description: Emphasizes the need for clear reserved powers for states to ensure a balance of authority and prevent federal overreach.

item.title: Virginia Ratifying Convention XIIV
item.description: Points out that many important rights were omitted from the Constitution’s enumeration and must be safeguarded through amendments.
